evidence: Ingested data/training_data.csv into Hopsworks feature group leakage_check (v1) and computed per-label statistics on the platform via Trino over the offline (Delta) store. f4 shows near-deterministic class separation: for label=0, mean(f4)=0.0003 with std=0.152; for label=1, mean(f4)=2.505 with std=0.161 (Cohen's d ~16). All other features f1,f2,f3,f5,f6 have nearly identical class means (~0.0-0.2) with std ~1, i.e. no separation. A single threshold f4>1.2 classifies all 800 rows perfectly (100% accuracy); max(f4|label=0)=0.596 and min(f4|label=1)=2.064 leave a clean non-overlapping gap. This perfect predictiveness is characteristic of a post-outcome-derived (leaking) feature, so f4 is the leak.
